    * Identical costs between sparse and dense solvers
    * Marginal constraint satisfaction for both solvers

author: Peyman Mohseni Kiasari <peyman.mohseni.kiasari@uwaterloo.ca>
message:
Update plot.py

## Added Arrow Annotation Feature to `plot2D_samples_mat` Function

### Changes:

1. **New Parameter `draw_arrows`**: Introduced an optional boolean parameter `draw_arrows` to the `plot2D_samples_mat` function. When set to `True`, this parameter allows users to plot arrows in the middle of the lines connecting source and target samples. This helps to visually identify the direction from source to target.

2. **Arrow Placement**: The arrows are strategically placed at the midpoint of the lines for clear visualization.

3. **Arrow Properties**: The color and alpha (transparency) of the arrows match the lines they are associated with, ensuring visual consistency.

### Motivation:

The addition of the arrow annotation feature enhances the visual representation of the connections between source and target samples. Especially in cases where directionality matters, these arrows provide a clearer understanding of the flow from source to target.

### Code:

The main code changes involve:
- Calculating the midpoint of the line segments.
- Using the `plt.annotate` method to draw an arrow at the calculated midpoint.

### Example Usage:

```python
plot2D_samples_mat(xs, xt, G, draw_arrows=True)
```

[BLD] Add support for NumPy 2.0 wheels (#629)

* build: Add support for NumPy 2.0 wheels [build wheels]

* Add numpy>=2.0.0 to build-system requires to build NumPy 1.x and 2.x compatible
  wheels.
   - c.f. https://numpy.org/doc/stable/dev/depending_on_numpy.html#numpy-2-0-specific-advice
   - As NumPy 2.0 is Python 3.9+, also need to conditionally support 'oldest-supported-numpy'
     for Python 3.8.
* Remove wheel from build-system requires as it is never required and injected
  automatically by setuptools only when needed.
   - c.f. https://learn.scientific-python.org/development/guides/packaging-classic/

* build: Remove setup_requires metadata

* Remove setup_requires as it is deprecated and should defer to PEP 517/518.
   - c.f. https://learn.scientific-python.org/development/guides/packaging-classic/#pep-517518-support-high-priority

* fix: Use np.inf to avoid AttributeError

* Avoids:

  AttributeError: `np.infty` was removed in the NumPy 2.0 release.
  Use `np.inf` instead.

  AttributeError: `np.Inf` was removed in the NumPy 2.0 release.
  Use `np.inf` instead.

author: nathanneike <nathanneike@outlook.de>
message:
Add checkpoint/resume functionality to EMD solver

Implements pause and resume capabilities for the EMD (Earth Mover's Distance)
solver, allowing long-running optimizations to be interrupted and continued
from their exact state.

Changes:
- Modified EMD_wrap() signature to accept checkpoint parameters for saving
  and restoring complete internal solver state (flow, potentials, tree structure)
- Added saveCheckpoint(), restoreCheckpoint(), and runFromCheckpoint() methods
  to NetworkSimplexSimple class in network_simplex_simple.h
- Extended emd_c() Cython wrapper to handle checkpoint dictionaries with 12 fields
  (10 arrays + 2 scalar arc counts)
- Added 'checkpoint' and 'return_checkpoint' parameters to emd() Python API
- Includes search_arc_num and all_arc_num scalars in checkpoint to preserve
  initialization state required by start() method

Tests:
- Added test_emd_checkpoint() for basic save/resume functionality
- Added test_emd_checkpoint_multiple() for multiple pause/resume cycles
- Added test_emd_checkpoint_structure() to verify checkpoint field integrity

performance improvement sinkhorn lpl1

 - instead of updating individually for each target examples, update for all target examples at once using numpy functions. This allows for a faster computation (for me, divided by 4 on 3000*100 random matricies and random labels in [0,1]).

 - if I understoud correctly, a value of -1 in the array labels_a meant that we didn't have a label for this example. But in machine learning, we often encounter the binary case where we say we have the positive class (+1) and negative class (-1); thus with a dataset like this, the algorithm wouldn't work as expected. I replaced the default value for 'no label' to '-99' instead of '-1', and I added a parameter to modify it.

    * Marginal constraint satisfaction for both solvers

  optimal transport when the cost matrix has many infinite or forbidden edges.

author: Pierre Chambet <pierrechambet@gmail.com>
message:
Fix Wasserstein distance formula in user guide (#798)

The exponent p was incorrectly placed as a subscript on the norm
(denoting the p-norm) instead of a superscript (raising the cost
to the p-th power).

Before:  ||x_i - y_j||_p   (p-norm of the displacement)
After:   ||x_i - y_j||^p   (norm raised to the power p)

The standard definition of the Wasserstein-p distance uses an
arbitrary ground metric d raised to the p-th power:

    W_p(a,b) = ( min_gamma  sum_ij  gamma_ij * d(x_i, y_j)^p )^{1/p}

Also switched to \left( ... \right) for properly scaled delimiters.

Fixes #779

author: Pierre_Chambet <pierrechambet@gmail.com>
message:
Fix Wasserstein distance formula in user guide

The exponent p was incorrectly placed as a subscript on the norm
(denoting the p-norm) instead of a superscript (raising the cost
to the p-th power).

Before:  ||x_i - y_j||_p   (p-norm of the displacement)
After:   ||x_i - y_j||^p   (norm raised to the power p)

The standard definition of the Wasserstein-p distance uses an
arbitrary ground metric d raised to the p-th power:

    W_p(a,b) = ( min_gamma  sum_ij  gamma_ij * d(x_i, y_j)^p )^{1/p}

Also switched to \left( ... \right) for properly scaled delimiters.

Fixes #779

author: LeoGautheron <leo_g_autheron@hotmail.fr>
message:
Speed-up Sinkhorn

Speed-up in 3 places:
 - the computation of pairwise distance is faster with sklearn.metrics.pairwise.euclidean_distances
 - faster computation of K = np.exp(-M / reg)
 - faster computation of the error every 10 iterations

Example with this little script:

import time
import numpy as np
import ot
rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
transport = ot.da.SinkhornTransport()
time1 = time.time()
Xs, ys, Xt = rng.randn(10000, 100), rng.randint(0, 2, size=10000), rng.randn(10000, 100)
transport.fit(Xs=Xs, Xt=Xt)
time2 = time.time()
print("OT Computation Time {:6.2f} sec".format(time2-time1))
transport = ot.da.SinkhornLpl1Transport()
transport.fit(Xs=Xs, ys=ys, Xt=Xt)
time3 = time.time()
print("OT LpL1 Computation Time {:6.2f} sec".format(time3-time2))

Before
OT Computation Time  19.93 sec
OT LpL1 Computation Time 133.43 sec

After
OT Computation Time   7.55 sec
OT LpL1 Computation Time  82.25 sec

message:
Merge pull request #40 from connectomicslab/python3

This PR is dedicated to the first upcoming release candidate of CMP3 (v3.0.0-RC1). In particular it integrates all the last major changes planned prior to its official release:

- Migration to Python 3 with major dependency upgrades

- Option to run Freesurfer recon-all in parallel and to specify the number of threads used by not only Freesurfer but also all softwares relying on OpenMP for multi-threading. 

- Reviewed connectivity graph files to better conform to the  [BIDS extension proposal on connectivity data schema](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ugBdUF6dhElXdj3u9vw0iWjE6f_Bibsro3ah7sRV0GA). 

- Maintenance works including bug fixes, code cleaning and rearrangement of files

- Use [Codacy](https://www.codacy.com) to support code reviews and monitor code quality over time.

- Use [coveragepy](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/coverage-5.2/)  in CircleCI during regression tests of the BIDS app and create code coverage reports published on our [Codacy project page](https://app.codacy.com/gh/connectomicslab/connectomemapper3/dashboard).

- Added new regression tests in CircleCI to improve code coverage:

author: Blake R. Johnson <blake.johnson@raytheon.com>
message:
Make Bokeh server process persist after quitting.

Writes the Bokeh server PID to file upon loading the server. When launching a
new experiment, we check for the existence of a running process on that PID, and
skip loading the Bokeh server if we find it.

An open issue is to figure out how/when to shut the Bokeh server down. Ideally,
it would timeout if it hadn't received any messages after XX seconds. Not sure
how to make that happen, though.

Also, this code does not "double fork" the Bokeh process. Consequently, if the
user sends SIGINT with Ctrl-C, that will shut down the Bokeh server. Not sure if
you want to think of that as a feature or a bug.

without unloading/reloading the libalazar library. This caused the
library to have a dangling socket reference that it would try to stuff
data into, but there would be no one listening on the other end. We
added a means to unregister all sockets to clean up properly.

--with @grahamrow

author: Daniel Ellard <dan.ellard@raytheon.com>
message:
removed some debugging code; tightened up waiting

if the total observed points taken by the output channels
sums to less than the total fake data injected (which the
X6 object knows, because it injected it), then wait for
a short period of time and then check again, ad nauseum.

Note that we assume that the points will eventually be taken:
there's no other way to break out of this loop except by
seeing all the expected data.  If we don't see it all, then
we go into an infinite loop.

due to assessing the ends of the neurites from a minor branch point,
e.g. of a tick, which put it under the threshold. Now we remove
the smallest tick, then recompute everything to ensure that the
topology remains intact.

author: William Silversmith <william.silversmith@gmail.com>
message:
fix: reduce influence of integer truncation on averaged downsamples

Iterative downsample_with_averaging has the advantage that each level
of downsampling is a fourth the size of the original mip level. However,
as most image datasets are integer types, we were previously losing up
to a unit of luminance on each mip level due to integer truncation.

While this is difficult to avoid for superdownsamples, we can avoid it
while maintaining this desirable logarithmic time complexity by averaging
floats and writing integers at each mip level, limiting the total loss
of pixel luminance to at most 1 across all mip levels in a given task.

author: ranlu <ranlu@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Reduce read requests when creating sharded skeletons and meshes (#156)

* Cache spatial info files

Because igneous download all spatial info file for every tasks, with
fixed number of segments per shard, the downloading request grows
quadratically with volume. This can blow up the cost for large dataset
if we are charged for read operations. Cache it so it only grows
linearly with volume.

* Add a frag_path parameter to save frag files somewhere else

To create shard files, we at least have to read each segment once. With
billions of segments this can be significant. Add a frag_path parameter
so we can save the fragment files locally or somewhere the read requests
are cheap.

* Add a cache option to control CloudVolume cache behavior

Cache is disabled by default

for z, and 11 for x and y. In ZI_MC_QUICK_INTERP the vertex position
is averaged as (v1 + v2) >> 1, however v1+v2 can overflow, so we do
(v1 >> 1) + (v2 >> 1) instead.

Additionally, I am now super suspicious of ints that are not uints
as they lose a bit of valuable precision so that's scrapped.

message:
Cache spatial info files

Because igneous download all spatial info file for every tasks, with
fixed number of segments per shard, the downloading request grows
quadratically with volume. This can blow up the cost for large dataset
if we are charged for read operations. Cache it so it only grows
linearly with volume.

message:
feat: fine tune gradient for dijkstra

Centerlines are much better using the PDRF alone but occasionally
using only the PDRF without the DAF added results in very low value
regions where the gradient collapses into floating point errors.

The intuition here is that using the naked DAF overpowers the PDRF
and distorts the centerline, but only a small gradient is necessary
to correct collapsed regions. Therefore, we normalize the DAF so that
it provides a continuous small gradient that won't overpower the PDRF.

message:
perf: 32-bit Triangle Representations for Meshes (#49)

* refactor: add PositionType and LabelType template to cMesher

* wip: trying different template configurations

* wip: compiles but ImportError

* wip: successfully compiled a Mesher32

* wip: meshes appearing, but distorted and flattened

* fix: use correct unpack parameters for 64 and 32 bit vertex representations

* feat: Mesher class with automatic type selection

* fix: need to invert renumbermap

{ orig: newval } is being accessed like remap[newval]...

* fix: annotate a few more types, expand 32bit x,y fields by one bit

* fix(Mesher): save bit of precision in z

In 32-bit, single bits of precision matter as we only have 10 bits
for z, and 11 for x and y. In ZI_MC_QUICK_INTERP the vertex position
is averaged as (v1 + v2) >> 1, however v1+v2 can overflow, so we do
(v1 >> 1) + (v2 >> 1) instead.

Additionally, I am now super suspicious of ints that are not uints
as they lose a bit of valuable precision so that's scrapped.

* fix: correction to 32-bit shifts

* fix: masks should correspond to field width

They aren't all the same size in 32 bit mode.

* fix: finer restriction on mesher dimensions for 32-bit

* fix: need to distinguish between in-place and right-side masks

* fix: add validated boundaries to Mesher32 vs 64 selection

* docs: describe precision error in comment

refactor: change bits_in_field to xshifts and yshifts

This makes the 64 bit and 32 bit code consistent.

* perf: add float simplifier mode (previously always double)

* refactor: clarifying the role of variables, whitespace, flexible masks

* feat: MeshTask gets object_ids and progress arguments

message:
fix: close the stargates

Large loops get fused at a centroid which may not be located
inside the loop proper. This creates a radial structure with
many edges from the central vertex to the loop that I call a
"stargate".

If the distance from a selected central
vertex to the outer ring is greater than the EDT radius of the
central vertex, cut the ring using a single edge.

Edge selection could be done in a more intelligent way, but this
is better than the stargates.
